parsed.g: Get the order ID of the newest pending order
P_t: Navigated to the Magento Admin Dashboard
R_t: Navigate to the Sales > Orders section
Sort orders by date to identify the newest pending order
Extract the order ID of the newest pending order
parsed.e_t: The agent is on the Magento Admin Dashboard (http://172.185.52.29:7780/admin/admin/dashboard/). The page shows the dashboard with a top navigation menubar containing links to DASHBOARD, SALES, CATALOG, CUSTOMERS, MARKETING, CONTENT, REPORTS, STORES, SYSTEM, and FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS. The SALES link (node [590]) points to a dropdown anchor (#). The dashboard displays Last Orders showing order IDs 299 (Sarah Miller, $194.40), 65 (Grace Nguyen, $190.00), 125 (Matt Baker, $151.40), 136 (Lily Potter, $188.20), and 230 (Ava Brown, $83.40). These are recent orders but their statuses are not shown on the dashboard. The page has not navigated away from the dashboard — the click on SALES [590] appears to have opened a dropdown menu rather than navigating to a new page.
C: The agent must filter orders specifically by 'Pending' status to find the correct order
The newest pending order must be determined by order date, not just order ID

F_t.cause: The SALES link URL is a hash anchor (http://172.185.52.29:7780/admin/admin/dashboard/#), meaning it opens a dropdown submenu rather than navigating to a new page. The ground-truth DOM still shows the Dashboard page unchanged after the click, confirming no navigation occurred.

K_t: The SALES menu item (node [590]) is a dropdown trigger with URL ending in '#', requiring a submenu item click to navigate to Orders
The dashboard 'Last Orders' table shows recent order IDs: 299, 65, 125, 136, 230 — but these are not filtered by 'Pending' status
Order details pages follow the pattern: http://172.185.52.29:7780/admin/sales/order/view/order_id/{id}/
The Orders list page is likely accessible via Sales > Orders submenu after expanding the SALES dropdown
